chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAlī, from Ibrāhīm ibn Isḥāq, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Ḥammād, from Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah, from one of the two (Imams) عليهما السلام, regarding the saying:
Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “and none knows its interpretation except Allah and those firmly rooted in knowledge.”

So Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله is the most excellent of those firmly rooted in knowledge. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, taught him all that was sent down to him of the revelation and the interpretation, and it is not for Allah to send down to him something without teaching him its interpretation.
And his successors after him know all of it. As for those who do not know its interpretation, when the knower among them speaks with knowledge, Allah answered them by His saying:
“They say: We believe in it; all of it is from our Lord.”
And the Qur'an contains the specific and the general, the decisive and the allegorical, the abrogating and the abrogated; so those firmly rooted in knowledge know it.

key_terms.التَّنْزِيلِ: the revealed wording sent down by Allah
key_terms.الرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ: those firmly grounded in knowledge, possessing established divine understanding
key_terms.تَأْوِيلَهُ: its inner interpretation or ultimate meaning
key_terms.مُتَشَابِهٌ: having resemblance or ambiguity requiring proper interpretation
key_terms.نَاسِخٌ: that which abrogates a previous ruling or wording-context

ai.seo_question: Who are the ones firmly rooted in knowledge in Qur'an 3:7 according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the verse about those firmly rooted in knowledge refers foremost to Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله, whom Allah taught both the revelation and its interpretation. It also states that his successors know the entirety of that knowledge, and that the Qur'an includes different categories of verses whose proper understanding belongs to those firmly rooted in knowledge.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Ali, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq, from Abdullah Bin Hammad, from Bureyd Bin Muawiya, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) regarding the Words of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic
[3:7] but none knows its interpretation except Allah, and those who are firmly rooted in knowledge:

‘So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> is the most superior of the ones firmly rooted in the knowledge. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic had Taught him<sup>saww</sup> the entirety of what had been Sent down upon him<sup>saww</sup> from the Revelation, and it was not so that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Revealed something unto him<sup>saww</sup> and not Teach him<sup>saww</sup> its interpretation.

And his<sup>saww</sup> succesors<sup>asws</sup> from after him<sup>saww</sup> knew all of it, and those that are not knowing its interpretation, when the scholar said regarding them with knowledge, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Answered them with His<sup>azwj</sup> Words
[3:7] We believe in it, it is all from our Lord; and none do mind except those having understanding

. And the Quran (has Verses which are) Particular, and General, and Decisive, and Allegorical, and Abrogating, and Abrogated. So the ones<sup>asws</sup> firmly rooted in the knowledge are knowing it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from ‘Abdallah ibn Ali from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq from ‘Adallah ibn Hammad from Burayd ibn Mu‘awiya who has narrated the following from either one of the Imams (a.s.) about the words of Allah, Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most gracious.
“No one knows its true interpretations except God and those who have a firm grounding in knowledge . .” [3:7].

The Holy Prophet is the best among the people well-grounded in knowledge. Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most gracious, taught him all that He had revealed to him in the form of original text and in the form of interpretations. Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most gracious, would not reveal anything to him that he would not know the meaning thereof.
The successors of the Holy Prophet (s.a.) after him knew all revelations. As for those who do not know the interpretations thereof, when the scholar speaks to them with knowledge,
they say, “We believe in it, for all of this is from our Lord.”
The Holy Quran consists of specific, general, clear, not so clear, abrogating and abrogated statements. The people who are well-grounded in knowledge know all of the Holy Quran.”
